reviewQuestions.question: Transitive reobservation callback lock order
reviewQuestions.coordinatorFinding: The project journal lock is retained. Runtime completes browser observation before calling the final registry guard; its inner commit checks only local deadline/control, then takes the Wake store lock for exact timer/delivery/target CAS. No paired-target mutex is acquired under registration lock. Prepared registry resolution loads metadata and checks Git identity without taking a second registration lock.

reviewQuestions.question: Separate pre-submit observations
reviewQuestions.coordinatorFinding: ProjectStore retains the OS project lock; exact journal/request/native-owner/event/target/policy are rechecked before the existing durable SUBMITTING fence and submit ACK. Existing tests cover changed selection/owner, sibling isolation, unknown outcome and duplicate suppression. Concurrent policy or registration updates are not claimed impossible. Collection and binding retain their separate owner/source witness checks.

reviewQuestions.question: Supervisor component wildcard interpretation
reviewQuestions.coordinatorFinding: Actual Windows PowerShell5 and PowerShell7 read the exact frozen identity function. literal[1] and literal1 remain distinct, case aliases match and spaces/plus/parentheses are accepted. Windows directory-name syntax excludes wildcard star/question-mark components. This does not prove resistance to malicious concurrent directory replacement.

reviewQuestions.question: Legacy monitor and mutable helper boundaries
reviewQuestions.coordinatorFinding: Matching legacy mutex reservations are supported. Pre-fix monitors through another case spelling remain unqualified and require verified quiescence before upgrade. The function extraction reads trusted local source, not a handle-pinned hostile file. No production activation or new same-user adversarial trust model is claimed.

harnessFailuresPreserved.reason: Windows PowerShell inherited the bundled PowerShell7 PSModulePath and could not load Get-FileHash. A first case-sensitive environment-key removal missed the uppercased Windows mapping. Case-insensitive removal for the child restored default host module discovery.
harnessFailuresPreserved.scope: Private diagnostic harness only. Canonical release-recovery helpers already hash through .NET; no product helper regression was established by this test.

limitations: Literal-path behavior is proved for the tested normal local filesystem only; malicious directory/helper replacement is not tested.
Existing legacy case-alias migration still requires known-owner quiescence; no arbitrary process termination is authorized.
These coordinator tests and source references are not an independent release verdict or installed startup qualification.
